stories.title: ‘Six, seven, maybe more preventable deaths’: Queensland’s LNP faces reckoning over broken health system
stories.summary: A government in office for more than two years is finally forced to take responsibility and seemingly no longer able to blame its Labor predecessors Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast At the beginning of another Queensland parliamentary sitting week, anonymous sources were out in force, this time background briefing against the state’s Labor leader, Steven Miles. It is no great revelation to observers of Queensland politics that Miles, still seemingly bruised from his election loss two years ago, has struggled to find his feet as opposition leader. Many wondered why he wanted to stay on after the party’s drubbing in 2024. Some of Labor’s factional whisperers were telling anyone who would listen that the former premier’s leadership would come to an end in the weeks before Christmas. Continue reading...

stories.title: Australian neo-Nazis among far-right groups raising hundreds of thousands via global crowdfunding platform
stories.summary: GiveSendGo has been accused of facilitating the financing of extremism, but the platform says it does not ‘condone racism, discrimination, hate speech, or violence of any kind’ Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian neo-Nazis have raised hundreds of thousands of dollars on the global crowdfunding platform GiveSendGo, which has been accused of facilitating the financing of hate and extremism. Of the 68 Australian fundraisers on the site, the White Australia party has raised the fourth-highest amount of money with $200,000 for its high court battle to overturn its ban as a designated hate group . stories.title: Louisiana man charged with killing woman on hiking trail and murdering co-worker with crossbow
stories.summary: Jared Schurr arrested in Mississippi after Lizeht Rodriguez and Woodrow Scott died in otherwise unrelated killings A man recently strangled a woman to death whom he did not know along a hiking trail north of New Orleans – then killed his co-worker with a crossbow two days later before being arrested in Mississippi after a police chase, authorities allege. Jared Schurr, 36, faces counts of second-degree murder in the killings of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, and Woodrow Scott, 37, on 11 and 13 November, respectively, investigators said on Saturday. stories.title: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave the UK’ over plans to house asylum seekers nearby
stories.summary: Local MP says legitimate criticisms of asylum housing plans are being co-opted by opposition parties ‘stirring up racial discord’ Residents of a Suffolk village have voted to “leave the UK” in a referendum held in response to government plans to house 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former military base. Approximately 500 people in Barnham were eligible to take part in the symbolic vote on Saturday. There were 257 votes for independence, 16 against and one spoiled ballot. Continue reading...

stories.title: Trump orders contractors to check with White House over any congressional inquiries
stories.summary: Anticipating flood of Democratic requests, US president issues executive order in attempt to stymie oversight efforts Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to an executive order issued late Friday. The companies must also coordinate with the White House and US agencies on “appropriate responses” to any such requests, the order says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns, their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended. Continue reading...

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that triggered widespread panic in the city of Guasave.
